mechanism: External ETH transfer happens before state update; the recipient re-enters the same function while the accounting still shows the pre-withdrawal balance, draining funds repeatedly.
root_cause: State (balances) updated after an external call to a user-controlled address (checks-effects-interactions violation).
preconditions: attacker contract receives ETH from a vulnerable function
state update occurs after the external call
no reentrancy guard or send-order lock
exploit_sequence: attacker deposits a small amount
calls withdraw which sends ETH first
receive() re-enters withdraw before balance is zeroed
repeats until contract drained
remediation: Update state before external calls (CEI); use reentrancy guards; prefer pull-payment patterns.

mechanism: Read-only reentrancy: during an external callback the victim contract reads accounting state that is temporarily inconsistent, letting the attacker swap/claim against stale prices.
root_cause: A view/claim function reads state that another function mutates across an external call boundary.
preconditions: defensible function performs external call before finalizing state
other contracts read the same state during the callback window
exploit_sequence: attacker enters vulnerable function
re-enters a read-only consumer (e.g., pool get_virtual_price or router)
acts on inconsistent intermediate state
profits from the price/accounting skew
impact: Protocol-wide loss as consumers act on corrupted state.
remediation: Reentrancy guards on view-style entry points consumed by other contracts; finalize state before external calls.
code_evidence: claim() { externalCall(); updateReward(); } // reward read mid-call

mechanism: A state-changing function lacks an authorization check, so any caller can invoke privileged behavior (mint, mintTo, setOwner, upgrade, sweep).
root_cause: Missing onlyOwner/onlyRole modifier or caller validation on a privileged function.
preconditions: no modifier and no explicit msg.sender check
exploit_sequence: attacker calls the unguarded function directly
gains ownership/mints/sweeps funds
impact: Full takeover or direct loss of funds.
remediation: Apply access modifiers to all privileged functions; add tests asserting they revert for non-privileged callers.
code_evidence: function setOwner(address o) external { owner = o; } // no check

source: OpenZeppelin upgradeable plugins docs — initializer guidance
mechanism: Proxy implementation logic runs uninitialized: either the implementation lacks an initializer guard or the proxy storage was never initialized, letting anyone call initialize() and become the owner/admin of the freshly-deployed proxy.
root_cause: initialize() without initializer modifier (or implementation left initialized/uninitialized) in a proxy deployment.
exploit_sequence: attacker front-runs or finds the uninitialized proxy/implementation
calls initialize() to set themselves as admin
upgrades or drains the contract
remediation: initializer modifier on all initialize functions; _disableInitializers() in implementation constructors; initialize immediately after deployment.
code_evidence: function initialize(address admin) { admin = admin; } // no initializer

mechanism: A shared library contract holding wallet logic is killed (selfdestruct) by an unauthorized caller, bricking every wallet whose delegatecall target points at it.
root_cause: Library/proxy target left with an unguarded kill/ownership function; wallets permanently delegatecall into it.
preconditions: attacker initializes or claims ownership of the library
exploit_sequence: attacker claims the library ownership (init re-run)
calls kill()/selfdestruct
all dependent wallets permanently bricked
impact: Permanent loss of access to all funds held by dependent wallets.
remediation: Guard library kill functions; make delegatecall targets verified and immutable; initialize targets atomically.

source: SWC Registry SWC-104 / unchecked call return
mechanism: The return value of send/call/transfer (or a token transferFrom) is ignored; failures proceed silently, corrupting accounting or skipping fees.
root_cause: Low-level call return value discarded (no require/assert on the boolean).
exploit_sequence: make the transfer revert (token that returns false or fails)
contract continues as if it succeeded
accounting desync / free mint / underpaid purchase
impact: Silent accounting corruption; free extraction of value.
remediation: require() every low-level call and token return value; use SafeERC20.

source: bZX / Mango attacks — oracle manipulation postmortems
mechanism: Protocol prices are derived from a manipulable on-chain spot (AMM pool reserves or self-reporting contract) — an attacker pushes the spot price with a large swap (often flash-loan funded) and borrows/trades against the skewed price.
root_cause: Spot price from low-liquidity on-chain source used for value accounting without manipulation resistance.
preconditions: price read from a pool balance pair or single on-chain source
low-cost way to move that source (buy/sell, oracle update)
value can be extracted using the inflated price
exploit_sequence: flash-loan large amount
push the spot/oracle price out of range
borrow/collateralize against inflated value
unwind, repay flash loan, keep profit
remediation: Manipulation-resistant oracles (TWAP/median, Chainlink with sanity bounds), spot-price feeds never used for value-bearing decisions alone.

mechanism: Governance executes a malicious proposal in the same transaction it passes; voting power is flash-loaned, so an attacker can propose, pass, and execute a fund-drain in one block.
root_cause: No timelock between proposal approval and execution; voting power snapshot on-chain and borrowable.
preconditions: votes can be acquired temporarily (flash loan)
exploit_sequence: flash-borrow governance tokens
pass malicious emergency proposal
execute it in the same tx
steal reserve funds and repay the loan
impact: Treasury drained in a single transaction.
remediation: Timelock between vote and execution; flash-loan-resistant snapshot; delay after large voting-power changes.
code_evidence: execute(proposalId) after quorum met in same block

source: SWC Registry SWC-114 / ERC20 approve race
mechanism: ERC20 approve is a race: a spender can front-run an approve change and spend both the old and new allowance (also: approve to zero then set must be atomic).
root_cause: Non-atomic allowance overwrite semantics of approve().
preconditions: victim calls approve to change the amount
exploit_sequence: victim broadcasts approve(newAmount)
attacker front-runs it: spends old allowance in-flight
after approve confirms attacker spends the new allowance too
impact: Double spend of allowance beyond intended amount.
remediation: Use increase/decreaseAllowance-style APIs; treat approve to a nonzero value from a spender with existing access as unsafe.

mechanism: Division before multiplication (or early rounding) truncates amounts so that small deposits/shares map to zero or let the first depositor steal later deposits via share-price inflation.
root_cause: Integer truncation order: value/total rounded down before scaling, or share-price manipulable at low liquidity.
preconditions: share math like shares = amount * supply / totalAssets with tiny totalAssets or rounding down of user amounts
exploit_sequence: first depositor supplies 1 wei unit price shares in
attacker donates tokens to inflate share price
next depositor's shares round to zero, donation skimmed
impact: Loss of depositor funds; free value extraction for the attacker.
remediation: Round in users' favor; scale before dividing; minimum share bounds; guard first-mint inflation.

mechanism: An upgrade path (signature set/guardian action or proxy upgrade) can be satisfied by spoofed/incomplete verification: the contract accepts an upgrade transaction without verifying that the old verification layer has approved/signed, letting attacker-supplied code become the implementation.
root_cause: Upgrade/verification functions accept partial or attacker-controlled inputs (missing signature check / unverified guardian set).
preconditions: guardian/multisig verification path with a hole
attacker can submit the upgrade tx
exploit_sequence: attacker submits crafted upgrade/set-inputs transaction
the missing verification lets it through
bridge logic replaced or drained
remediation: Verify every signature set and upgrade path; require previous-owner authorization semantics; time-lock upgrades.
code_evidence: function submit(bytes memory data) { upgrade(data); } // no verify

mechanism: Contracts compute amounts using pre-transfer balances, but fee-on-transfer or deflationary tokens deliver less than requested — accounting then overstates holdings, letting users over-withdraw.
root_cause: Assumption that transferred amount equals requested amount; balance deltas never re-measured.
preconditions: uses requested amount for bookkeeping rather than balance-diff
exploit_sequence: deposit a fee-on-transfer token
contract credits full amount, received less
withdraw against inflated credit
repeat to drain underlying
remediation: Measure balance-before/balance-after; support only standard tokens or explicit fee-tolerant math.
code_evidence: IERC20(t).transferFrom(msg.sender, this, amt); shares = amt; // overcredits

source: known Solidity pitfalls — storage layout in upgradeable proxies (OpenZeppelin docs)
mechanism: Appending or reordering state variables in an upgrade shifts storage slots relative to existing data, making the new logic read the old layout as different variables — funds/admin/roles misinterpret storage.
root_cause: Storage layout compatibility broken between implementation versions.
exploit_sequence: deploy v2 with shifted layout
upgrade the proxy
v2 misreads slots (owner slot now reads some other var)
admin/role checks misbehave
impact: Authorization corruption; bricked or drained proxies.
remediation: Use gap() reserved slots; never reorder or change existing variable types; use ERC-7201 namespaced storage for new vars.

source: donation/first-depositor attacks on share pools (public audit corpus)
mechanism: Direct transfers (donations) to a share-pool contract inflate totalAssets without minting shares, letting the first depositor steal later deposits because share price jumps after a donation.
root_cause: Pool accounting based on raw balance() but assets enter without minting shares.
preconditions: share price = totalAssets/totalShares computed from balance
exploit_sequence: attacker deposits tiny amount (1 wei share)
donates a large amount to inflate totalAssets
next depositor's shares round to nearly zero
attacker redeems and keeps both
impact: Next depositor loses their entire deposit.
remediation: Virtual shares/offset; mint dead shares on first deposit; measure assets via internal accounting not raw balance.
